## Fourth document: the Cyrus Minecraft Feature Roadmap (owner-attached, 2026-10-09)
This one is about **what Cyrus can create** (the capability ladder), so it is the closest match to the owner's goal. Its main ideas: a **Mod Specification + Capability Router** (decide plugin vs data pack vs resource pack vs future client mod, tell the user the limits, and plan before spending tokens), a **Data Pack Studio** (recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, worldgen), a full **asset pipeline** (textures, models, sounds, packaging, hybrid JAR + pack delivery), **Cyrus Test Flight** (isolated real Paper server + MockBukkit + a Mineflayer-style bot, honest per-check statuses), a **visual Gameplay Designer** (item designer, ability/event graph, quests, bosses, GUIs, minigames), **server-aware context, diagnostics and a Mod Pack Builder**, and a later **Fabric client-mod** path. Its recommended next feature: Spec + Router, then Data Pack Studio.

**How it maps onto the other three documents**
- ModSpec = the Master Plan's `CyrusTaskSpec` (section 4.1) = the asset manifest we need. **One schema**, owned by one ticket, with an `artifacts` field (plugin / data pack / resource pack / client mod) and an `assets` field (models, textures, sound events). This is also where the router's decision is stored.
- Test Flight = Master Plan CYR-012/013/014 (MockBukkit, disposable Paper smoke lane, functional tests) plus the Mineflayer bot lane. Same work; the roadmap adds the bot and the honest-status table.
- Verified component library = the unmerged `feature/cyrus-v6-library` pattern library. Same work; the roadmap names the components worth having (custom-item identity, cooldowns, GUI pagination, config + migrations, boss phases, quests).
- Targeted edits + revisions = Master Plan CYR-020/023 (manifest, minimal patcher).
- Server Context / Diagnostics / Mod Pack Builder / Version Upgrade Assistant / Mod Doctor = new, later (post-launch design topics, not research steps now).
- Fabric/NeoForge client mods = new, explicitly LATER. Everything the owner listed (creatures, HUD, biomes) must first be sorted into "doable on a vanilla client" vs "needs a client mod"; that is research Step 3.

**Where its order conflicts with the owner's current priority, and the resolution**
The roadmap puts assets 5th (after Spec/Router, edits/components, Data Packs) and the Designer 6th. The owner now wants assets (creature model + textures + multiple sounds, automated, then editable) as the headline. Resolution: **Spec + Router goes first because assets need it** (the router is what decides "this request also needs a resource pack and a model", and the spec carries the asset IDs), but keep the first Router minimal: route among {plugin, plugin + resource pack, data pack} and disclose limits. Then the asset slice, then Data Pack Studio, then Test Flight growth, then the Designer. Launch gates stay ahead of all of it.

**New research needs it adds (folded into the steps below)**
- Step 3b: Data Pack Studio (per-version schemas/formats for 1.21.x and 26.x, validators and open-source generators and their licences, how Paper loads datapacks, load tests). Biomes, structures, recipes, loot, advancements land here.
- Step 3 also answers the HUD/UI question honestly: which HUD/GUI effects are vanilla-possible (boss bar/action bar, font glyph tricks, custom inventory GUIs with pack fonts, shaders) versus client-mod-only.
- Step 7 gains a Test Flight sub-question: Mineflayer and MockBukkit support for 26.x, cost of a disposable Paper server per build on the build host.
- Steps 3-4 must verify the roadmap's own claims (it is a proposal; its source links are unopened).

**Scope warning.** Together the four documents describe years of work. The plan's job is to pick the order, not to commit to all of it. Everything not on the minimal path (Designer, Server Context, Mod Pack Builder, client mods, differentiators like screenshot-to-mod and structure generator) is parked as a later design topic and gets research only when it becomes next.

## [SUPERSEDED by the two-week FULL plan below] One-week version (owner: "we can do this in a week", 2026-10-09)
Day 1 = the day weekly usage resets. A week fits ONE strong vertical slice, not all four documents. Research is done just-in-time inside each day (only the questions that day needs), not as a separate phase.

| Day | Build | Just-in-time research | Owner actions needed | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Launch gates: confirm hardened scan is live; per-build version/scan record; launch-flag guard. 26.x decision | Step 1 (versions), Step 2 (gap audit) | Run VM 88001 update; say yes/no to the 26.x image (JDK 25 + Gradle 9) | We can prove what built each mod; 26.x scope decided |
| 2 | ModSpec + minimal Capability Router (plugin / plugin + resource pack / data pack) + asset manifest in the project record | Step 3 (what is vanilla-possible), 3b (datapacks, light) | Review the ModSpec fields | A prompt like "Glock handgun with sounds" routes to plugin + pack with limits shown |
| 3 | Texture slice: LLM-written pixel spec -> existing renderer -> validated pack; Nxeon hosts the pack and sets `resource-pack` + sha1 on the server through the Mods engine; custom item end to end | Step 6 (texture, light), pack format for the pinned version | **Test in a real Minecraft client** | Pack loads in a real client; item shows the custom texture |
| 4 | Sound slice: SoundSpec, tag the 514-file library, synth presets, server-side Ogg encode, `sounds.json`, several events per mod (fire, reload, hit, etc.) | Step 5 (sound, light) | Customer-facing sound licence text; real-client sound test | Plugin plays the right sounds in a real client |
| 5 | Creature slice (banshee): archetype rig + skin + attack/hurt/death/idle sounds. Realistic target: custom skin + full sound set on a vanilla-model mob, and display-entity model only if Step 4 research clears a library | Step 4 (models), only what Day 5 needs | Real-client check | Banshee with its own look and 4+ sounds installs and plays |
| 6 | Studio editing: open a mod's textures and sounds in the studios, edit, rebuild + re-push the pack, keep revisions; simple data-pack path (recipe/loot) | Step 7 (quality), light | Review the editing UX | Customer can change a texture or sound and see it on the server |
| 7 | Test Flight lite (disposable Paper smoke test on node-2), eval run on asset prompts, docs, release package | Step 7 sub-question: test tooling for 26.x | Approve deploy; decide flag flips | Evidence bundle; deploy block ready for the owner |

**In the week:** launch gates, Spec + Router (minimal), pack delivery, custom item (the Glock), multi-event sounds, a banshee reskin with full sounds, asset editing, data-pack basics, Test Flight lite.
**Not in the week:** visual Gameplay Designer and ability graph, quest/boss/minigame designers, custom HUD shaders, biomes and structures beyond datapack basics, Fabric/client mods, Server Context/Mod Pack Builder, the other five games, a full 3D animated creature library, 26.x beyond the Day-1 decision (unless the image change is trivial).

**What can stop it**
- **Weekly usage.** This week hit 99% on mostly diagnosis and planning. A build week of this size is heavier. Stay lean (Sonnet, no parallel agents, small steps) and the owner should check the allowance and whether extra usage is available.
- **Owner-only steps** block days: the VM 88001 update and image rebuild, deploys, flag flips, real-client tests, the sound licence text.
- **Real-client testing** cannot be done from the server; each asset day needs someone with Minecraft open.
- **Day 5 creature** depends on a model-library choice that is unresearched; if it fails the fallback is skin + sounds only.

## FOUNDATION PRINCIPLE: Minecraft work is the base for every future game (owner decision, 2026-10-09)
Everything built for Minecraft in this plan is designed as the **foundation for the other games** (Terraria, Valheim, Palworld, Rust, Zomboid and later ones). Build the platform once, validate each game separately. Rule for every ticket: *if it is not Minecraft-specific, it goes in the shared core, behind an interface; if it is, it goes in the Minecraft adapter.*

**Shared core (game-agnostic, built once)**
- Mod spec + capability router (same schema; each game declares its own routes/artifact types).
- Project manifest + revision store (asset IDs, hashes, licences, known-good revision).

| **Bosses** | Strong base mob (or model-engine mob) + Paper `BossBar` + phases/abilities/loot in plugin; arena via structure/command. | V | none specific | High |
| **Abilities / projectiles** | Paper events + scheduler, raycasts, Snowball/Arrow/Display-entity projectiles, particles, sounds, potion effects. | V | Scheduler differences Folia/Paper (UNVERIFIED). | **High** |
| **Commands** | Brigadier Commands API via lifecycle event (VERIFIED lifecycle URL); clients get tab completion. | V | Command API moved from plugin.yml commands to lifecycle; 26.x unverified (E-versions). | High |
| **Music / ambience / SFX** | `sounds.json` + .ogg in pack; `jukebox_song` datapack registry for discs; ambient via scheduled `playSound` / biome ambient sounds in datapack. | V | `sounds.json` stable. | High (assets from Sound Studio). |
| **Biomes / structures / worldgen** | Datapack JSON: `worldgen/biome`, `configured_feature`, `placed_feature`, `structure`, `template_pool`, `noise_settings`, `dimension`, `dimension_type`. Server syncs registries so a vanilla client can join (UNVERIFIED but well established). Structure NBT files in `structure/`. Biomes: custom fog/sky/water/grass colours, spawn tables, features, music. | V for biomes, structures, ore/tree features, new dimensions using vanilla noise/terrain tech; **not** V: new block types, custom sky *rendering* (dimension_type `effect` limited to vanilla set, UNVERIFIED), custom biome *names* on the client (F3 shows id) | Worldgen datapack JSON changes most between versi

## 2. Client-mod-only list (cannot be done on a vanilla client)
- New block types with arbitrary properties, new entity types with native models/animations, true custom blocks beyond the reusable-state pool.
- Arbitrary HUD widgets/GUI screens with real controls and free layout (Dialog API gives only form-like screens).
- Custom keybinds, mouse capture, camera control, client-side prediction (smooth gun recoil).
- New dimension sky/cloud/fog *renderers*; custom shaders that need new vertex formats; post-processing outside the shipped pipeline mechanism (UNVERIFIED how much `post_effect`/core shaders allow on 26.x).
- Anything requiring new client code paths (new GUI sliders, minimap, custom render of player model).
Fabric/NeoForge client-mod route: out of scope for Cyrus today; Nxeon would need to ship players a client mod pack = adoption friction.

## 3. Libraries and licences (can Nxeon depend on / bundle?)
| Library | Area | Licence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BetterModel** | bbmodel mobs/props/player models, animations, auto pack | **MIT** VERIFIED (github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel); Bukkit servers + Fabric; 1.21.4 to 26.3.x | **Adopt**: can be bundled or required as a dependency; keep MIT notice. Best fit for the "banshee" mob use case. |
| **CraftEngine** (Xiao-MoMi) | custom blocks/items/furniture/GUI/recipes via config | **GPL-3.0** community edition; premium edition sold separately VERIFIED (github.com/Xiao-MoMi/craft-engine) | **Avoid as a bundled dependency** (GPL); study as design reference only. Running it as a separate server plugin the customer installs is legally cleaner than linking, but Nxeon-generated jars must not link to its API. |
| **Oraxen** | items, blocks, glyphs/HUD, pack hosting | Paid (Spigot/BuiltByBit), source visible with LICENSE.md terms, "forks only for PRs" VERIFIED (github.com/oraxen/oraxen) | **Avoid**: cannot redistribute. |
| **Nexo** | items, blocks, armor, furniture, auto pack | Paid; docs say 1.21.1 to 1.21.11 (VERIFIED via search result excerpt, nexomc.com docs) ; GitHub page 404; terms UNVERIFIED | **Avoid** (paid, per-server licence, 26.x unclear). |
| **ModelEngine R4** (Ticxo) | bbmodel mobs, MythicMobs integration | Paid, free demo limited; reported expensive; lists 1.19.4 to 26.2 on a re-host site (UNVERIFIED, mirror sites unreliable) | **Avoid** bundling; BetterModel is the open equivalent. |
| **MythicMobs** | mob skills/AI config | Free base + paid Premium (UNVERIFIED; official page not opened, GitLab link needs login) | **Avoid** dependency; Cyrus generates Java behaviour itself. |
| **ItemsAdder** | all-in-one | Paid (UNVERIFIED) | Avoid. |
| **Blockbench** (editor) | model/animation authoring, bbmodel format | GPL-3.0 UNVERIFIED; the *file format* is JSON (reading it is fine) | Reference only: write our own bbmodel emitter, never embed the editor. |
Net: only BetterModel is a clean commercial dependency. Everything else (items, blocks, HUD glyph, pack builder, menus) should be a small **Cyrus runtime library** owned by Nxeon, because Cyrus-generated plugins are compiled against a frozen classpath and need a stable, versioned helper API anyway.

## 4. Ranked build order (value vs effort)
1. **Pack hosting + server-pushed pack + correct per-version pack_format** (S-M). Unblocks everything; installer currently marks packs unsupported.
2. **Items with custom art** via `item_model`/CMD, food/tool/weapon/armor components, recipes, sounds (M). Texture Studio output already exists in `lib/cyrus/textures`; biggest "wow per effort"; weapons/guns high AI reliability.
3. **Abilities/projectiles/bosses/commands/enchant/advancements** with vanilla-only assets (S, mostly prompt + sheet work).
4. **Custom mobs on BetterModel** (L): bbmodel emitter from Texture Studio spec, 1.21.4+ only, multi-sound set. Highest marketing value; heavy generation risk.
5. **Glyph-based HUD + GUI menus helper lib** (M): fonts/negative-space helper, Dialog where available; no core shaders.
6. **Datapack studio** for biomes/structures/enchants (L, see A2).
7. **Custom blocks/machines** (L): state-pool allocator + display-entity furniture; maintenance-heavy.
8. **Core-shader effects** (L, last or never): fragile across 26.x and client mods.

## 5. Gaps / not determined
Writable-registry list; Nexo/ModelEngine/MythicMobs official licence text; exact 26.x client behaviour for shaders and font glyph limits; Dialog API Paper availability; 1.21.1 item_model route (must use legacy CMD).

20932:### Cyrus engine core (R0)
## Cyrus Test Flight (R0)

"Test Flight lite" (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r0`, **not wired into the build path, nothing deployed**): boot ONE throwaway real Paper server for one registry version on node-2, load the given plugin jars / datapacks, run the checks, tear it down, return a JSON report. Master plan 4.6.

**Files**
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/runner.js`: the runner (plain Node, no deps; runs on node-2 as root). `node runner.js run <resolved-spec.json>` prints the report JSON; `node runner.js setup 21|25` fetches + verifies a pinned JDK.
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/lib.js`: its pure helpers (log matchers + default ignores, plugin.yml-from-jar reader, `plugins` reply parser, RCON wire format, server.properties, resolved-spec validation).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/fixtures/`: `hello` (positive control, `/tfhello`), `broken` (throws in onEnable), `datapack-tf_smoke` (one function), `build.sh` (javac `--release N -proc:none` against a classpath file + reproducible `jar --date`, same as the build service).
- `lib/cyrus/testflight/types.ts` (spec/report types), `spec.ts` (`validateSpec`, `resolveSpec`, `requiredStages`; fail closed on the registry), `summary.ts` (`summarize`, `mergeSummaries`, `describe`), `client.ts` (`runTestFlight`, `sshRemote`, injectable `Remote`).
- Spec extras (added with pack delivery): `files` (small text files placed under `plugins/` before boot, max 16 x 64 KB) and per-RCON-check `writeFile` / `waitMs` (replace a file, optionally wait up to 30 s, then send the command), so a plugin's config reload can be tested. Both validators (`spec.ts`, `lib.js`) confine paths to `plugins/<plain segments>`.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-testflight.test.ts` (pure, 24 tests), `test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts` (real node-2 runs, run by hand: `tsx test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts all --out r.json`).
- Registry: `paperBuild`/`paperServerSha256` now also pin the **server** jar for 1.21.11 (build 132, Fill STABLE). A version without a server pin cannot be test-flown (1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 today).

**Checks, in order** (each `pass` / `fail` / `not_run` with evidence lines; a check never passes unless it ran):
1. `boot_done`: a `Done (Xs)!` line within `bootSec` (default 180).
2. `plugins_enabled`: per plugin (name read from the jar's plugin.yml / paper-plugin.yml): log has `Enabling <name> v`, no `Error occurred while enabling`, no `Disabling <name>` before stop, and the RCON `plugins` listing shows it green (red = disabled = fail).
3. `startup_log_clean`: default matchers (ERROR/FATAL level, exception headers, enable/load errors, datapack load errors) over the log up to the Done line. Spec `logMatchers` replace them (an empty list is refused), `logIgnore` adds ignores. The two built-in ignores cover only noise the sandbox itself causes (no internet: Mojang public-key fetch, Paper version fetch); ignored lines are counted in the evidence.
4. `rcon_checks`: spec commands with `expect`/`expectNot` substrings (colour codes stripped), plus an automatic `datapack list enabled` check per datapack. stop/restart/op/deop/reload are reserved.
5. `clean_stop`: `stop` over RCON (stdin fallback), exit code 0 within `stopSec`, no matcher hits during shutdown.
6. `no_leaks`: our java PID gone, no process anywhere carrying this run's `-Dnxeon.testflight.run=<runId>` marker, no listening port in the reserved range (checked inside the netns and on the host).

**Verdict** (`summary.ts`, pure): required stages come from the spec we sent (boot, log, stop, leaks always; plugins if any plugin; rcon if any command or datapack; plus `requireStages`), not from the runner's flags. Any required fail = `failed`; any required stage missing / `not_run` / "pass" with no evidence = `incomplete`; `busy` and `error` reports are never success. `success` is true only for `passed`.

**Safety on node-2** (shared build host): one flight at a time (`flock -n` on `TF_ROOT/testflight.lock`; a second caller gets `status: "busy"` immediately, exit 75); the server runs in a private network namespace (`unshare --net`, loopback only: no internet, cannot reach or collide with host ports) as uid/gid 65534 with `no_new_privs`, `nice 10`, `-Xmx1g` max, SerialGC, 2 visible CPUs, an RSS watchdog (default 1800 MB) and a hard timeout (runner `totalSec` default 420 + an outer `timeout -s KILL`); kills are only ever by exact PID after re-checking the marker in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`; the run dir and the upload inbox are always removed. Paper jars are fetched from the Fill API only when Fill's sha256 equals the registry pin, then pre-patched once (`paperclip.patchonly`, `bundlerRepoDir`) into a root-owned cache the server cannot write. Plugin jars are re-hashed on node-2 against the hash the invoker computed.

**node-2 layout** (`TF_ROOT=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight`, about 1.5 GB): `jdk/21` (Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, sha256 ce79869e...bcfaee94) and `jdk/25` (Temurin 25.0.4.1+1, sha256 dbb69839...215cf41e), both checked against the Adoptium API; `dl/` (tarballs by sha256); `paper/<sha256>/` (server jar + pre-patched libraries); `runner/` (the invoker pushes `runner.js`/`lib.js` whenever their hash differs from the repo); `runs/` (per-flight dirs, removed); `inbox/` (uploads, removed; `inbox/fx` holds the fixture jars); `reports/<runId>.json`; `classpath/1.21.11.txt` (+ `.sha256`) and `gradle-home/` from resolving the 1.21.11 compile classpath with the template (Gradle 8.14.3 on JDK 21, 24.7 s, 850 MB peak).

**Measured on node-2 (2026-10-10, RAN)**, Done-line wall time from JVM spawn and peak RSS (VmHWM), tiny flat world, `-Xmx1g`:

| Version | JDK | Plugin | Boot (wall) | Paper "Done" | Peak RSS | Whole flight (runner) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | HelloR0 + datapack | 10.6 s | 9.2 s | 803 MB | 13.5 s |
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | TfBroken | 10.6 s | 9.3 s | 762 MB | 12.4 s |
| 26.1.2 b74 | 25 | none | 10.4-10.8 s | 9.3-9.4 s | 722-729 MB | 12.2-16.8 s |
| 1.21.11 b132 | 21 | TfHello + datapack | 18.0 s | 16.6 s | 878 MB | 20.4 s |

One-off per Paper jar: download + pre-patch about 5 s. End to end from the primary over ssh adds about 5-10 s (each ssh connection to node-2 costs about 2.2 s; the invoker uses two: runner hash check, then one call that uploads a tar of artifacts + spec and runs the flight). The research estimate (20-45 s boot, 1.0-1.5 GB) was pessimistic: plan for about 20 s and 1 GB per flight. Capacity: one flight at a time by design, so about 3 flights a minute on 26.x and 2 on 1.21.11, using about 1 GB RAM and up to 2 cores while it runs.

**Results of the real runs (RAN)**: HelloR0 on 26.2 passed all 6 checks (`/hellor0` answered, `function tf:hello` ran, `file/tf_smoke` enabled); TfBroken on 26.2 failed `plugins_enabled` and `startup_log_clean` with the enable-error line, the `IllegalStateException` header and the red `plugins` entry as evidence (boot/stop/leaks still pass); TfHello compiled with JDK 21 `--release 21` against the template-resolved 1.21.11 classpath passed all 6 on Paper 1.21.11; a second flight started 4 s into another came back `busy` with every check `not_run` while the first passed. After the runs: no process with the marker, no port in 47100-47199, empty `runs/` and inbox (verified). An earlier 1.21.11 run correctly FAILED its log check because `-Dcom.mojang.eula.agree` logs at ERROR level on 1.21.11; the flag was removed (eula.txt is written instead).

**NOT RUN / not covered**: no player or bot joins (PlayerJoin listeners, GUIs, the resource-pack prompt are untested; `resourcePack` is only written to server.properties and reported `exercised: false`); no MockBukkit or Mineflayer scenarios; Paper 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 have no server pin; the runner runs as root on node-2 and only the server drops privileges (no container/cgroup limits; a cgroup memory cap via systemd-run would be the next hardening step).

**Hand-off: how the portal/worker would call it** (not wired yet): from a worker job (never a request handler; a flight takes 15-30 s), after a successful build: `const { summary, report } = await runTestFlight({ version, plugins: [{ localPath: jarPath, sha256 }], datapacks, rcon: [{ command: "plugins", expect: [pluginName] }, ...specChecks] })`. Store `report` (it carries the runner hash, JDK + Paper sha256s, artifact sha256s) next to the build's engine-release record, and show `describe(summary)`; only `summary.success` may show a "booted on Paper X" badge. On `busy`, requeue with backoff (do not run in parallel). Run it from the primary (the worker host) via `sshRemote()`; the build VM 88001 is not involved. For a version matrix, run sequentially and combine with `mergeSummaries`.

**Owner actions**: none to deploy. Decide later (a) whether to gate publishing on `summary.success` once wired, (b) whether to pin Paper server builds for 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 so they can be test-flown, (c) whether to add cgroup limits (systemd-run scope) on node-2 for the flight. Cleanup when no longer needed: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight` (about 1.5 GB) and `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/r0-26x` (about 2 GB, the 26.x lane probe, still used as the source of the HelloR0 fixture jar and the 26.2 classpath).

content.content:
### Cyrus engine core (R0)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r0` (2026-10-10). Plan: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/MASTER-PLAN.md` sections 4.1-4.3, 4.10 and R0; code audit `G-gaps.md`. **Nothing here is wired into the build pipeline yet** (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts` is unchanged): builds still run exactly as before, and the new tables stay empty until a later slice writes to them.

**Version-support registry** (`lib/cyrus/versions/registry.{ts,json}`, R0 day 1). One row per Minecraft version: family, `javaRelease` (21 for 1.21.x, 25 for 26.x), `status` (supported / preview / legacy / blocked), `buildable` (true only for what the build service compiles today: 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11), exact `paperCoordinate` (null for 26.x until a stable build is pinned), resource/data pack formats (null = unverified, consumers fail closed) and capability flags (`itemModelDefinitions` 1.21.4+, `dialogApi` 1.21.7+, `adventure5`). `resourcePackFormat()` replaces the old `packFormatFor` guesswork. The same JSON is readable by the plain-Node build service.

**Layout.** `lib/cyrus/engine-core/` is the game-agnostic core and must never name a game; `lib/cyrus/adapters/` holds the per-game facts.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `engine-core/spec.ts` | ModSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateModSpec` + `migrateSpec` + `modSpecJsonSchema()` |
| `engine-core/modspec.v1.schema.json` | the portable JSON Schema contract; regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus-modspec-schema.ts` (a test fails while it is stale) |
| `engine-core/identifiers.ts` | namespaces, identifier formats, glyph codepoints, `detectCollisions` (pure) |
| `engine-core/revisions.ts` | manifest validation, `diffManifests`, engine record (pure) |
| `engine-core/store.ts` | the only writer of the four tables (server only) |
| `engine-core/router.ts` | deterministic capability router |
| `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | plan-tier asset gate + router downgrade |
| `adapters/types.ts`, `adapters/minecraft.ts`, `adapters/index.ts` | `GameAdapter` contract, adapter #1, `getAdapter(game)` |

**ModSpec v1.** `schemaVersion` (1), `game` (adapter id), `target.version` (must be in the adapter's version registry; a preview version is valid but warns `version_not_buildable`; `blocked` is an error), `namespace` (the project's reserved `nx_<8>`), `summary`, `routes` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod), `requirements` with stable ids `REQ-1..` and priority must/should/could, `nonGoals`, `constraints`, `assets` slots `{ id, kind: texture|sound|model|ui, purpose, source, requirementIds }`, `tests` (acceptance plan `T-1..`: compile / scan / boot / functional / manual, `covers` REQ ids), `install` (side, restartRequired, clientSteps, notes). Unknown keys are rejected. Validation never throws: it returns `{ ok, spec | errors, warnings }`, each issue `{ path, code, message }` (codes include `missing_schema_version`, `schema_too_new`, `no_migration`, `unknown_game`, `unknown_version`, `duplicate_id`, `unknown_requirement`; warnings `untested_requirement`, `route_unsupported`, `asset_kind_undeliverable`). Migrations: `SPEC_MIGRATIONS[n]` rewrites version n to n+1; empty while v1 is the only version. Asset `source`: `generate`, `library`, `upload`, `edit` bring new or changed content (gated); `existing`, `imported` keep what the project holds (never gated).

**Projects and revisions** (`store.ts`). `createProject({ userId, game, title?, rootBuildId? })` reserves a unique namespace (`namespaceFromSeed(projectId)`, retried with a new seed on a clash; `rootBuildId` optionally links a ModBuild chain, unique). `addRevision(projectId, { kind: generated|edited|imported|asset, manifest, spec?, modBuildId?, engine?, status?, message?, expectedHeadId? })` validates the spec (and that its game/namespace are the project's), the manifest (`[{ path, sha256, role }]`, safe relative paths, unique, stored sorted) and the engine record (prompt version, sheets with hashes, rules version, scanner hash, image digest, model, toolchain: only what is known), then appends under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the project row: gap-free `seq`, `parentId` = previous head, head moves; `expectedHeadId` gives an optimistic `stale_head` refusal. `setRevisionStatus` is the one allowed change: pending -> passed | failed, once; a pass becomes `lastPassingRevisionId` only if it is newer than the current one, so a later failure never loses the last good revision. `getHead`, `lastPassing`, `listRevisions`, `diffRevisions` (added / removed / changed files), `revertTo(projectId, targetId)` = a NEW `revert` revision copying the target's spec, manifest, build link and status (`revertOfId`, `engine.revertOf`); history is kept. `recordAsset` stores content-addressed assets (same content twice = one row). Errors are `EngineStoreError` with a `code`.

**Immutability in the database.** Section 2 of the manual migration adds a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger on `CyrusRevision`: any change to content columns raises, and `status` may only go pending -> passed | failed. `prisma db push` does not create triggers, so it is applied by hand with the migration (the DB test applies the same SQL to its throwaway DB). Deletes stay allowed (account/project deletion).

**Namespaces and identifiers.** Kinds `item`, `model` (path with `/`), `sound` (dotted), `permission` and `config` (`nx_x.a.b`), `command`, `recipe`, `glyph`; `buildIdentifier(ns, kind, key)`, `parseIdentifier`, `validateIdentifier(kind, id, ownNamespace)`. `CyrusIdentifier` is unique per (namespace, kind, key); `reserveIdentifier` is idempotent. Glyphs: each namespace has a home block of 256 codepoints in the supplementary Private Use Areas (U+F0000 and U+100000 planes, 510 blocks; the crowded BMP PUA is not used); a full block moves on to the next. `codepoint` is unique across ALL projects, so Mod Packs cannot collide on glyphs. `detectCollisions(records)` (pure) reports duplicate ids (case-insensitive), duplicate codepoints and invalid ids across any set: a project, a pack, a server.

**GameAdapter** (`adapters/types.ts`, MASTER-PLAN 4.10): artifact types per route with availability `available | planned | unsupported`, default route, toolchain profile (compiler, release per version, scanner path), knowledge source, version list with capabilities, asset delivery per kind, install rules, test lane, maturity (`planned | template | beta | stable`) and the router's `routeRules`. **Minecraft** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`) reads the version registry and `lib/cyrus/games/minecraft.ts` and changes neither; maturity `beta`; only `plugin` is available today; `resourcePack` and `dataPack` are `planned`; `clientMod` is `unsupported`; all four asset kinds deliver via a server-pushed resource pack (planned); boot/functional tests `planned`.

**Capability router** (`router.ts`, no AI call). `routeSpec(spec, adapter, { prompt?, gate?: { plan } })` matches the adapter's rules against summary + requirements + asset purposes + prompt (never non-goals or constraints) and asset kinds, and returns `routes`, split into `available / planned / unsupported`, a `label` (`plugin`, `plugin+resourcePack`, `dataPack`, ... or `clientMod-unsupported`), `buildableNow`, `limits` (`info | warn | block` with plain-English text) and the matched rule ids. Minecraft limits: custom blocks, free-form HUD widgets, keybinds and custom sky need a client mod; native entity models need a client mod (skinned vanilla mobs / display entities instead); Dialog API needs 1.21.7+; item models need 1.21.4+; worldgen needs a restart; a preview or unknown target version blocks; planned routes say "not built yet". With `gate`, the asset gate runs first and strips gated assets (warn limits `asset_gate:<id>`), and a gated asset named only in words adds a `<rule>:plan` notice instead of a route.

**Plan-tier asset gate** (`asset-gate.ts`, owner decisions). `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`: `create` and `edit` (also automatic generation inside a build, library picks and uploads) need `saka` for sound and `all` for texture; `model` and `ui` follow texture (top plan). `keep`, `install`, `export`, `rebuild`, `import` (your own mod) and `compose` (Mod Packs) are never gated, for any plan or none. Unknown plan / token state -> `plan_unknown` denial for create/edit only (fail closed). `normalizePlan` is the one mapping of plan names (`all` = `yakko` = "All models"; free, katara, saka). `gateSpecAssets` lists denials (the build service request must run it again), `downgradeSpecAssets` strips gated slots with a customer-visible reason and leaves requirements in place. Wiring into `gateBuild`/`create.ts` is left for the asset slice (R1): builds carry no spec or assets yet, so there is nothing to gate there today.

**Tests.** `test/cyrus-engine-core.test.ts` (pure: spec, migrations, JSON Schema file, identifiers, collisions, manifests, adapter, router, the 40-case gate matrix and more). `test/cyrus-engine-store-db.test.ts` (opt-in, throwaway DB only): `devhost db push`, then `devhost run --lock -- env CYRUS_ENGINE_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-engine-store-db.test.ts`.

**Deploy (owner).** Review and apply `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql` (four new tables + the trigger; no ALTER/DROP of anything existing). Nothing in the app reads the tables yet, so the migration can land before or with the code.

### Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`)

Customers pay for Cyrus's AI in **Cyrus tokens**. Design and every number with its reasoning: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/ECONOMY.md`. **Preview-only until launch:** Setting `cyrus_tok_live=false` means only private-preview accounts (`lib/preview-access.ts` "modbuilder") earn grants, see the checkout line, the balance or the plans. Everyone else sees and earns nothing (`lib/cyrus/tokens/access.ts tokensActiveFor`, fails closed). Cyrus is labelled **Beta · Minecraft Java only** wherever tokens appear.

**Unit.** 1 token = $0.002 of the build service's measured `costUsd` (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), times a model multiplier (Katara 1, Saka 1, Yakko 1.25), min 5 per build that reached the AI. Typical builds: Katara ~34 tokens (ChunkMirror 80), Saka ~52 (complex ~95; Sonnet-5 tier builds 150-338), Yakko ~214 simple. Customers never see a USD figure per token or a model family name (`test/cyrus-tokens-economy.test.ts`).

**Where tokens come from.**
- **Game servers**: on purchase `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`, on every paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)`; monthly $ = what was actually paid per month. Prepaid N-month terms earn per month (cap 12). Lots expire after 90 days (or term + 30 d). $0 trial starts earn the initial grant on the first paid renewal. Idempotent `gs:<serverId>:initial` / `gs:<serverId>:renew:<periodStartISO>`. Abuse caps: 3 initial grants per account per 30 days, 3,000 unexpired server tokens held. **Only games Cyrus builds for earn** (and get the checkout line): the server's game family must be a `status: "live"` game in `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (`lib/cyrus/tokens/games.ts earnsCyrusTokens`), today Minecraft Java only (`minecraft`; `bedrock` and other games earn nothing). Making a game live there makes its servers earn. `lib/cyrus/games.ts` on this branch is a byte-identical copy of the file on `feature/cyrus-modbuilder` (commit c19b512f86), so the two merge cleanly; if that file changes before the merge, take the modbuilder version. Hooks: `lib/game-order.ts placeGameOrder` (post-commit, `safeGrantPurchase`), `worker/billing.ts commitRenewal` (the single "renewed" exit, every sweep/card/PayPal/admin path) and `lib/actions.ts renewNow` (`safeGrantRenewal`). Never throws into an order or renewal.
- **Plans** (Stripe Billing subscriptions, monthly): Katara $4.99 = 750 tokens/month (Katara), Saka $19.99 = 3,500 (Katara, Saka), All models $49.99 = 10,000 (all three). Every paid invoice grants (`plan:<invoiceId>`), so renewals stack; each month's plan tokens last 3 months from their grant (`cyrus_tok_plan_rollover_months`), so at most 3 months stack. (A first design trimmed to "3 x the current plan" on each invoice; a real test-mode run showed a replayed old invoice could then expire paid tokens, so the cap is by age.) Upgrade = immediate proration (`always_invoice`, tokens in proportion to the money collected); downgrade = at the next renewal; cancel = at period end, plan tokens stay 30 days (Katara only) then expire; past_due keeps the unlock 3 days. Refunds (`charge.refunded`) take back that purchase's unspent tokens pro rata.
- **Top-ups**: one-off Checkout payment, $5-$100, 120 tokens/$, 12-month expiry, no unlock (`topup:<sessionId>`).
- **Admin**: grant / revoke / comp a tier at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`.

**Models.** No plan = Katara only; Katara plan = Katara; Saka plan = Katara + Saka; All models = all three; admin comp can raise it. Enforced server-side in `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` (403 `model_locked`).

**Spending** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/builds.ts`, called from the build route and `lib/modbuilder/store.ts syncBuild`): before the `ModBuild` row exists, `gateBuild` resolves the model, checks the unlock and **holds** the high end of the estimate (or the whole balance if that still covers the typical cost; else 402 `insufficient_tokens`; daily cap 5,000 tokens, 1,000 for accounts younger than 7 days, 429 `daily_cap`). When the build turns terminal, `settleBuildTokens` spends the **actual** cost and releases the rest: succeeded / refused / cancelled pay actual, our-side failures are free (3 per rolling 7 days, then actual), never-started builds release everything. A cost above the balance is a write-off, never a negative balance. Estimate table: `cyrus_tok_reserve_table`.

**Ledger** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts`, the only writer). Additive models: `CyrusTokenAccount` (locked `FOR UPDATE` by every operation; `balance`/`reserved` are caches), `CyrusTokenLot` (source, remaining, expiry; spends draw soonest-expiring first), `CyrusTokenLedger` (append-only, `idemKey` UNIQUE: grant / purchase / reserve / spend / release / refund / expire / revoke, with `source`, `sourceRef`, `buildId`, `balanceAfter`), `CyrusTokenReservation` (one hold per build), `CyrusPlan` (the subscription mirror; `tier` = paid entitlement from invoices, `priceTier` = what bills next). Due lots are expired inside every operation, and by the worker.

**Stripe** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/billing.ts`). Prices are found by lookup_key `cyrus_plan_<tier>_v1` (override ids: `cyrus_tok_price_*`); create them with `scripts/cyrus-tokens-stripe-setup.ts` (TEST mode; refuses a live key unless `CYRUS_STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE=1 ... --live`). Checkout uses the platform's custom "elements" UI inside the Cyrus modal; `return_url` = `/api/cyrus/tokens/return` (same idempotent fulfilment as the webhook). **Our sessions carry `cyrusUserId`, never `nxeonUserId`**, so `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` classifies them "unpaid" and the wallet/order engine can never treat a Cyrus purchase as a top-up (pinned by a test). `app/api/stripe/webhook` calls `handleCyrusStripeEvent` for every verified event: `checkout.session.completed`, `invoice.paid`, `customer.subscription.*`, `charge.refunded`; each re-fetches from Stripe and applies the current state. **Owner action for live:** enable `invoice.paid`, `customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted` and `charge.refunded` on the webhook endpoint (the reconcile below covers a missed event).

**Worker**: sweep `cyrus-tokens` every 5 min (`lib/cyrus/tokens/sweep.ts`): settles holds whose build finished, releases holds whose build vanished (>2 min) or is older than 3 h, expires due lots, reconciles active plans with Stripe at most hourly. Plans are also reconciled on a Cyrus page load (5-minute throttle).

**API** (all preview-gated with `modBuilderUser()`, 404 otherwise): `GET /api/cyrus/tokens` (state; `?history=1&before=` ledger page), `POST /api/cyrus/tokens/checkout {kind: plan, tier} | {kind: topup, cents}`, `POST /api/cyrus/tokens/plan {action: change|cancel|resume}`, `GET /api/cyrus/tokens/return?session_id=`, `GET /api/cyrus/tokens/checkout-line?monthlyCents&termMonths` (404 for anyone outside the economy and while impersonating).

**UI** (`components/cyrus-tokens/*`, styles `tokens.css`, `cyt-*` classes, self-contained). Integration contract for any Cyrus UI (mounts, `cyrusTokens` API, routes, error codes): `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/UI-CONTRACT.md`. Current mounts (Cyrus v4), one line each:
- `components/cyrus/CyrusApp.tsx`: `<CyrusTokensHost />` (modal: Plans / Top up / History, inline Stripe card form, post-checkout notice); in `create()` `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError(j)` + `cyrusTokens.refresh()`; the Cyrus Pro "Upgrade" opens the plans when the account is in the token economy.
- `components/cyrus/Switcher.tsx`: `<CyrusTokenChip />` after the New button; `<CyrusTokensMenuItem />` (balance + history) above the Pro card.
- `components/cyrus/Composer.tsx`: `<CyrusTokenEstimate />` replaces the USD estimate; `<CyrusModelLock />` in the model picker; `<CyrusModelPanelFoot />` replaces the "nothing is charged" footer.
- `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`: `<CyrusCheckoutLine />` in the game order summary, server-gated.

**Admin** `/admin/cyrus-tokens` (URL-only; billing area AND the preview allowlist, like `/admin/mod-builder`): liability (unexpired tokens and their AI-cost value), holds, 30-day spend vs real AI cost, plans and MRR, outstanding/granted by source, the economy table at the live settings, accounts, the latest ledger rows, grant / revoke / comp forms (audit-logged) and every `cyrus_tok_*` Setting with its default.

**Tests**: `test/cyrus-tokens-economy.test.ts` (formula, plan gating, settlement, margins, wallet isolation, brand voice) and `test/cyrus-tokens-ledger-db.test.ts` (opt-in throwaway DB: idempotent and concurrent credits, reserve/settle/release, overrun write-off, daily cap, races, FIFO + expiry, revoke vs holds, grants and their caps, the preview gate, build gate + settle, webhook replays, stacking, upgrade, rollover, cancel grace, refund, top-up replay).

### Cyrus admin portal: /admin/cyrus (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v6-admin`, NOT deployed)

The staff side of Cyrus in one place. **URL-only during the private preview** (no admin-nav entry, like `/admin/mod-builder`): the real signed-in account must be staff AND on the `modbuilder` preview list (`preview_access_emails_modbuilder`), else 404. Each tab and each write maps to an admin Area (`lib/cyrus/admin/perms.ts`): **fleet** (ADMIN) Overview, Builds, Library & safety, cancel / re-run; **billing** (BILLING + ADMIN) Users & tokens, refunds, grants, comps; **support** (SUPPORT + ADMIN) Community moderation and suspensions; **platform** (ADMIN) Games & models, networking review + kill switch, Audit & settings. A role only sees its tabs; a support or billing account opening `/admin/cyrus` lands on its first tab. The older `/admin/cyrus-tokens`, `/admin/cyrus-mods` and `/admin/mod-builder` pages are unchanged.

**Tabs.**
- **Overview** (`/admin/cyrus`): builds per day (30 d, by outcome; refusals and cancels counted apart from failures), success / fail / refused rates and avg / p95 build time by game and by model, queue depth from the service `/health`, a "Needs attention" list (builds running > 30 min, lost contact with the builder in 24 h, token holds left after a build finished, service down, open reports), and **AI cost vs tokens charged by model** from settled holds, valued at the top-up price and at the cheapest plan price (worst case). It is a reference margin: granted tokens earn nothing directly, the page says so.
- **Builds** (`/admin/cyrus/builds`, `/admin/cyrus/builds/<id>`): search by id, plugin, prompt or customer email; filter by outcome, model, game, period. Detail: prompt and change request, stages and events, AI calls (internal model names and cost), usage per stage (live from the service, 0.5+ only), safety findings, files, token hold / charge / refund and ledger rows, the project's versions. Actions: **cancel** (service cancel; "force" fails it locally when the builder is unreachable, then the normal settle runs), **refund tokens** (`creditTokens` kind `refund`, idempotent key `admin-refund:<buildId>`, at most what the build was charged, one per build) and **undo refund** (`revokeTokens` limited to that refund's lot, never below zero), **re-run** (the same request through `createModBuild` for the customer: a real build with AI cost and a normal token hold, confirm box required).
- **Users & tokens** (`/admin/cyrus/users?u=<email or id>`): list view with suspended accounts, safety refusals in 30 d, token accounts, comped tiers. Account view: balance / held / available, model tier and comp, plan, abuse flags derived from real rows (refusals, fail rate, daily cap reached, reports against posts, hidden posts, written-off cost), rate limits (24 h token cap vs used, builds running / last hour / last minute vs the code limits 2 / 20 / 3), grant / revoke / comp forms (the economy path), suspension, lots and ledger.

content.content:
## Cyrus data pack studio (R2)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r4` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 2b, 4.3, 4.11, R2 days 13-14; research `A2-datapacks.md`. **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** Two flags, both OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1` (portal: the build request may get the data pack route) and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL=1` (worker: a built data pack may be placed on a server). Off, every build request is byte-identical to before and no code touches a server. Data packs are **not plan-gated** (owner decision for composition features): no plan lookup happens for them. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the delivery uses the existing `MemberPlacer` from `lib/cyrus/modpack/install.ts`), no new tables, no foreign keys; assets go into the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "datapack"`.

**The flow.** Request -> capability router (data-driven words) -> the build service's AI writes **typed spec files** `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (never raw Minecraft JSON) -> the service validates + emits them with the GENERATED copy of the TypeScript code for the build's exact version, bounded repairs, drop-not-ship -> the portal re-validates and re-emits (the service is not trusted), records a revision + a datapack asset -> (flag) delivery into `<level>/datapacks/` + `minecraft:reload` (or a restart for enchantments).

### 1. Files (`lib/cyrus/datapack/`)
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `spec.ts` | DataPackSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateDataPackSpec(json, { version, namespace })` -> `{ ok, spec, errors, warnings, checks }` (never throws) + `canonicalJson` + `needsRestart` |
| `datapack.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema), generated (see below; a test fails while stale) |
| `versions.ts` | `dataPackFeatures(version)` (the verified per-version differences, below), `vanillaIds(kind, version)`, `isVanilla`, `missingIdReason` ("needs 1.21.11 or newer" / "was removed after 1.21.8") |
| `data/vanilla-ids.json` | ids ONLY (238 KB): items, blocks, entity types, enchantments, loot tables, advancements, recipes, item/block/entity/enchantment tags, loot function / condition / entry / number types, triggers, recipe serializers, enchantment effect components, mob effects, attributes, command roots, execute sub-commands, gamerules; grouped by a version bitmask. Generated by Mojang's data generator (`--reports --server`) from each pinned vanilla server jar on node-2 (sha256s in the file's `source`). No assets or content |
| `data/mcdoc-subset.json` | field tables derived from **vanilla-mcdoc** (SpyglassMC, MIT, commit `1528808766ccaaac10e64de002b05d3efc31a9a3`, attribution in the file): top-level keys, optional flags and `since`/`until` of every struct the emitters write |
| `mcdoc.ts` | resolves those tables per version (`dispatchFields`, `structFields`, `checkKeys`); outside the subset = null = not judged |
| `functions.ts` | the function SAFETY validator (allowlist, below) |
| `emit/{common,recipe,loot,advancement,enchantment,index}.ts` | per-version emitters; `buildDataPack(spec, ctx)` = validate -> emit -> static file check -> deterministic zip (`lib/cyrus/textures/zip.ts`: sorted entries, fixed timestamps) -> `{ zip, sha1, sha256, files, counts, apply: reload|restart, checks }` |
| `validate.ts` | `validatePackFiles(files, version)`: the static checker for emitted OR raw files (imports) |
| `route.ts` | `decideDataPackRoute` (build request), `routeWithDataPack` (router with the route switched on), `hasDatapacks`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` |
| `sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDatapacks` (portal re-validation / re-emission, cross-pack duplicates) |
| `deliver.ts` | `planDataPackDelivery`, `rebuildForDelivery`, `deliverDataPack` (flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`) |
| `import.ts` | `importDataPackZip`, `exportImported`, `checkRawResource` (edit/import library) |
| `service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |

Scripts: `scripts/cyrus/build-datapack-artifacts.ts [--check] [--out-dir DIR]` writes `services/modbuilder/datapack-spec.js` (bundled validator + emitter incl. zod and the id data, minified, 650 KB) and the JSON Schema; run it through `devhost run ... --out-dir /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/...` and copy back (devhost's next push deletes files written inside the node-2 copy). `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py ids|mcdoc` re-derives the two data files on node-2 (see 8).

### 2. DataPackSpec v1
`{ schemaVersion: 1, name, description, resources: [1-128] }`; `name` = file name. Every resource lives in the project's reserved namespace (`id` is only the path; engine-core identifiers gained the kind `resource` for `nx_x:a/b/c`, recipes use the existing `recipe` kind). References are full ids: own ones must exist in the spec, vanilla ones must exist in the TARGET version's id lists, any other namespace is refused.
- **recipe**: `shaped` (pattern 1-3 x 1-3, key), `shapeless` (1-9), `smelting` / `blasting` / `smoking` / `campfire_cooking` (experience, cookingTime), `stonecutting`, `smithing_transform`. Ingredient = id, `#tag` or a list of alternatives. Result = vanilla item + count + optional `name` (`minecraft:item_name`) and `lore` (a data pack cannot add items). Not supported: `smithing_trim`, special recipes, `crafting_transmute`.
- **loot_table**: kind generic/chest/entity/block/fishing/gift; pools (rolls = number / uniform / binomial, bonusRolls), entries item / tag (expand) / loot_table / empty with weight, quality; **functions subset**: set_count, set_damage, enchant_randomly, enchant_with_levels, set_name, set_lore, set_enchantments, explosion_decay, furnace_smelt, looting_bonus (= enchanted_count_increase with looting); **conditions subset**: random_chance, killed_by_player, survives_explosion, match_tool (items / tag), weather.
- **advancement**: parent (own or vanilla), display (icon, title, description, frame, background from the five vanilla tabs, toast/chat/hidden), **criteria subset**: impossible, tick, inventory_changed, consume_item, player_killed_entity, recipe_unlocked, recipe_crafted; requirements all|any; rewards experience / loot / recipes / function.
- **tag**: registry item / block / entity_type / function / enchantment; own tags, or additions to an EXISTING vanilla tag (`replace` defaults false; `replace: true` on a vanilla tag is refused); function tags: own, `minecraft:load`, `minecraft:tick`.
- **function**: a list of commands (+ `runOn: load|tick`, merged into the vanilla function tags).
- **enchantment**: description, supportedItems / primaryItems (tag or items), exclusiveSet, weight, maxLevel, min/max cost, anvil cost, slots, value effects (`damage`, `damage_protection`, `knockback`, `armor_effectiveness`, `item_damage`, `mob_experience`, `block_experience`, `repair_with_xp`, `smash_damage_per_fallen_block`; add / multiply / set, linear per level). Supported because the format of this subset was **verified identical on all six versions** (vanilla sharpness/unbreaking compared on every jar, and the custom enchantment loaded and was applied to an item on all six real servers). Enchantments are registry content: `apply = "restart"`.
- Not in v1: worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions: router warns), predicates / item modifiers as resources, vanilla loot-table or recipe overrides, macros.

### 3. Per-version differences (VERIFIED on the real jars, 2026-10-10)
Method: the vanilla data generator of each pinned server jar dumped the vanilla data pack; the same files were compared across versions, cross-checked with vanilla-mcdoc, then the emitted packs were booted (section 6).

| Difference | Versions | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Ingredients `{"item": id}` / `{"tag": id}` -> strings `"id"` / `"#tag"`; a list of alternatives may hold only item ids | 1.21.1 vs 1.21.2+ | vanilla `stick.json`, `fire_charge.json`, `netherite_sword_smithing.json`; mcdoc |
| Text in item components (`item_name`, `lore`) is a JSON **string** -> a text **object** | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `voluntary_exile.json` icon `minecraft:item_name` |
| Advancement background `minecraft:textures/gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone.png` -> `minecraft:gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone` | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `story/root.json` |
| `pack.mcmeta` `pack_format` -> `min_format` / `max_format` `[major, minor]` | <1.21.9 vs 1.21.9+ | mcdoc `pack.mcdoc`; registry formats 48 / 61 / 81 / 94.1 / 101.1 / 107.1 accepted by the real servers |
| Entity predicates `{"type": ...}` -> namespaced sub-predicates `{"minecraft:entity_type": ...}` | <26.2 vs 26.2 | vanilla `adventure/blowback.json`, `entities/zombie.json`; mcdoc `EntityPredicate` |
| Cooking results: single item (no count) -> item stack (count) | <26.1 vs 26.1+ | mcdoc `Smelting`; the validator refuses count > 1 before 26.1 |
| `smithing_transform.group` removed; `category` optional (26.2 vanilla drops it from many recipes) | 26.1+ / 26.2 | mcdoc; vanilla 26.2 recipes |
| Advancement icons: vanilla writes `count: 1` before 26.1, omits it after (both load; we mirror vanilla) | 26.1 | vanilla advancements |
| Loot `loot_table` entries reference by `value` (not `name`); tag entries need `expand` before 26.3 | all | mcdoc |
| Gamerules camelCase -> snake_case (`keepInventory` -> `keep_inventory`) | <=1.21.8 vs 1.21.11+ | `commands.json` of each jar |
| Item tag `#minecraft:enchantable/sword` removed, `#minecraft:enchantable/melee_weapon` added | 1.21.11 | vanilla tags (the validator caught it on the showcase) |
| Commands `rotate` (1.21.4+), `dialog`, `version`, `waypoint`, `test` (1.21.8+), `stopwatch`, `fetchprofile` (1.21.11+), `swing`, `unpublish` (26.x) | per version | `commands.json` |

### 4. Validation (quality-bar style checks: pass / warn / fail / not_run)
Spec checks: `schema`, `namespace`, `vanilla_ids`, `references`, `version_features`, `limits`, `function_safety`. File checks on the emitted (or imported) files: `mcmeta`, `mcdoc_fields` (unknown / missing keys per version), `value_shapes` (the format changes above), `emitted_ids` (recipe types, loot function / condition / entry types, triggers, items), `emitted_functions`, `not_checked` (resources outside the subset: listed, kept, never judged). The same report is stored with every datapack asset.

**Function allowlist** (`functions.ts`; functions run as the server at `function-permission-level`, 2 by default, up to 4 on some hosts). Allowed roots: advancement, attribute, bossbar, clear, clone, damage, data, dialog, effect, enchant, execute, experience/xp, fill, fillbiome, forceload, function, gamemode, gamerule, give, item, kill, list, locate, loot, me, msg/tell/w, particle, place, playsound, random, recipe, return, ride, rotate, say, schedule, scoreboard, setblock, spawnpoint, spectate, spreadplayers, stopsound, stopwatch, summon, swing, tag, team, teammsg/tm, teleport/tp, tellraw, time, title, trigger, waypoint, weather, worldborder; each must also exist in the target version's real command tree. Refused: op, deop, ban, ban-ip, banlist, pardon, pardon-ip, kick, whitelist, stop, save-off/on/all, reload, publish/unpublish, transfer, difficulty, defaultgamemode, setidletimeout, setworldspawn, seed, tick, debug, jfr, perf, test, fetchprofile, datapack, version, every namespaced root (`minecraft:op`, `bukkit:...`, plugin commands such as `lp`), macros (`$` lines, `function ... with`), `run_command` click actions, Command NBT, command / structure / jigsaw blocks, command-block minecarts and debug sticks anywhere, creative mode, `kill @e` without a type/tag/team/name/limit filter (`kill @a` warns), gamerules outside a gameplay list (both name styles). `execute ... run` and `return run` are unwrapped and checked to the end (nesting <= 12). Call graph over function / `execute if function` / function tags: no recursion, depth <= 8, calls only to this pack's own functions. Limits: 64 functions, 256 commands per function, 2048 commands and 256 KB per pack, 2000 chars per line, no line breaks, 64 commands per tick (tick functions and everything they call), 16 schedule commands (>= 1 tick, no `append` from tick functions), 4 `forceload add` (one chunk each). A summon in a tick function warns. Adversarial corpus: `test/fixtures/cyrus-datapack/function-corpus.json` (61 cases).

### 5. Router, build service, portal
- **Router** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`, `engine-core/router.ts`): rules `datapack_recipe`, `datapack_loot`, `datapack_advancement`, `datapack_tag`, `datapack_function`, `datapack_enchantment`, `datapack_content` route to `dataPack` with limits (vanilla items only; function allowlist; enchantments need a restart; client-visible looks still need a resource pack); `worldgen` is now a `warn` ("not built yet; needs a restart"). The adapter keeps `dataPack` as `planned`; `RouteOptions.routesOn` lets the host switch a planned route on (`routeWithDataPack` does it under the flag), so `plugin+dataPack` becomes buildable only where enabled. "Creepers drop diamonds" stays a plugin (vanilla loot overrides are not in v1).
- **Build request** (`lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts`, one line in `lib/modbuilder/create.ts`): with the flag on, matched words, `assets: ["datapack"]` or a base build that has data packs give `service.assets.datapack = true` and a project namespace (no plan lookup); `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.datapack = { route, matched, limits }`; a version without an emitter (26.3) gets a notice and no route. Flag off: nothing decided, nothing recorded.
- **Build service** (`services/modbuilder/{datapacks.js,datapack-spec.js,datapack-example.json,prompts.js,server.js,textures.js}`): `assets.datapack` parsed (non-boolean = 400; switched off with a note where the bundle has no emitter for the version); the `DATA PACK` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text, caches per version; the namespace is in the user turn); allow-list `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (max 4); a change build without the route keeps the base's specs byte for byte; every asset round runs `checkWorkspaceDatapacks` (the generated `buildDataPack` for the exact version + cross-file duplicates; HARD problems go back as `repair-asset`, bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`, then the spec is dropped with a customer-visible limitation); `assetResult.datapacks: [{ name, path, sha256, spec, pack: { sha256, bytes, format, counts, apply, emitter }, checks, warnings }]`, `datapackPromptVersion` `mb-datapack-2026-10-10.1`; `/health` lists `datapack`. Idempotent (revision by modBuildId, content-addressed assets). **No hosting**: data packs never go to clients, and the emitter is deterministic, so delivery rebuilds the zip from the stored spec and checks the recorded sha256 (`rebuildForDelivery`); nothing is public.
- **Delivery** (`datapack/deliver.ts`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`): one file `<level>/datapacks/nxeon-<namespace>-<name>.zip` placed through a `MemberPlacer` (production: `engineMemberPlacer`, the Mods engine, staged writes, state file), then `minecraft:reload` over the console for reloadable content, or `restartRequired` for enchantments. **Remaining steps (not wired)**: (1) a worker job after the jar install that loads the build's datapack assets, `rebuildForDelivery`, and calls `deliverDataPack` with `engineMemberPlacer` + the server's level name + an RCON/console `runConsole`; (2) removal = the placer's `remove` + reload when a mod is uninstalled; (3) the NxLabs page line; (4) a real-server check of `minecraft:reload` discovering a NEW pack file (Test Flight reserves `reload`; boot discovery and `datapack disable/enable` were verified).

### 6. Import / edit (`datapack/import.ts`, a library for the import agent)
`importDataPackZip(buf)` uses the bounded zip reader (5000 entries, 1 MB per entry, 32 MB total, ratio cap, CRC; unsafe names reported, never extracted; a single top folder is stripped) and converts what fits the subset for the pack's main namespace (recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags incl. vanilla-tag additions, functions; the Cyrus function header is recognised). Everything else stays a RAW resource with its bytes and a reason (enchantments, worldgen, predicates, structures, vanilla overrides, unknown fields or types, pack.png). `exportImported(imp, { spec?, rawEdits? }, { version, retarget? })` writes unchanged converted resources with their ORIGINAL bytes (exact round trip), re-emits edited ones for the version, keeps every raw file (edited ones replaced as text) and returns the file report; `checkRawResource` is the editor's live check.

Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite 995/995. `tsc` clean.

## Cyrus asset slice (R1)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r1` (from `feature/cyrus-r0`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 4.2-4.7 and R1 day 5 (textures); GAPS findings 5, 10, 15 and section D (Style DNA, quality bar). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** No real model build ran: the build service was exercised only through the fake-CLI pipeline test. Sounds are designed to plug into the same path next (see "Sound slice interface").

**The flow.** Build request -> server-side plan gate -> the build service's AI writes texture SPEC files (the existing DSL, Read/Write/Edit only) -> the service validates/renders/quality-checks them like code (bounded repairs) and returns them with the jar -> the portal re-validates, renders the deterministic pack through the version registry, hosts it, computes the Pack Loader entry and records a revision -> (flag-gated) the worker installs the Pack Loader and writes `packs.json` after the jar install.

### 1. Build request (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{kinds,plan,request}.ts`)
- What is REQUESTED: `body.assets` (`["texture"]` or `{ texture: true }`, a request only, never a permission), asset words the Minecraft adapter's route rules recognise in the prompt / change request (`item_model` -> texture, `custom_sound` -> sound), and kinds the base build already has (a change keeps working on them). Passed through `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` and `POST /api/cyrus/generate`.
- What is ALLOWED (`planBuildAssets`, pure): the R0 gate `canAsset(plan, kind, create|edit)` with the plan from the real lookup `tierOf(userId)` (CyrusPlan + admin override; a lookup error = unknown = fail closed), then the version (`itemModelDefinitions`, 1.21.4+; 1.21.1 is refused with "Custom textures need Minecraft 1.21.4 or newer ... Pick 1.21.4 or newer"), then `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY` (`texture: true, sound: false`). Owner rule: free/Katara no assets, Saka sound only, `all` (= Yakko) sound + texture. Only creating/editing is gated.
- Anything refused is a DOWNGRADE: the plugin is built anyway and one customer-visible notice per kind is stored in `ModBuild.cyrus.assets` (`requested`, `allowed`, `notices`, `projectId`, `namespace`; read by `readCyrusMeta`) and returned as `assetNotices` by the builds API. A change to a mod that has textures, on a plan that cannot edit them, says the textures are kept unchanged.
- For an allowed kind the chain's `CyrusProject` is loaded or created (`rootBuildId` = the chain root), so the build has its reserved `nx_<8>` namespace; a project that cannot be created fails closed (no assets, notice).
- **Byte-identical rule**: nothing requested -> no lookups, no project, no `assets` field; requested but refused -> still no `assets` field. Only an allowed request adds `assets: { texture, sound, namespace }` to the service call.

### 2. Build service (`services/modbuilder/{textures.js,prompts.js,server.js,texture-example.json}`)
- `POST /builds` takes `assets` (`textures.js parseAssetsRequest`): unknown fields, non-boolean flags or a namespace that is not `nx_<8>` are a 400; textures on a version without `itemModelDefinitions` in the service's copy of the registry are switched off (defence in depth; an unreadable registry = no textures anywhere). `/health` lists `features.assets: ["texture"]`. Asset builds are never deduped.
- Prompt: the system prompt gets the `CUSTOM TEXTURES` section only when textures are allowed (otherwise it is byte-identical to before; `PROMPT_VERSION` unchanged, texture builds record `mb-assets-2026-10-10.1`). It covers the DSL (sizes, palette, all ops), Style DNA (transparent background, 3-5 shade ramps lit from the top-left, flat areas, no noise or gradients, one dark outline colour for the whole mod, diagonal tools like vanilla), the checks it will be held to, "original art only", and the reference rule `meta.setItemModel(new NamespacedKey("<namespace>", "<texture name>"))` (no `setCustomModelData`, never send packs from the plugin). The namespace goes in the user turn (`assetsBlock`), so the section caches per version. Example spec: `texture-example.json` (= the golden ruby sword).
- Workspace allow-list: `assets/textures/<name>.json` survive only when textures are allowed. A change build without texture rights KEEPS the base's specs byte for byte (snapshot; edits are reverted, new files removed): keeping is never gated. The model keeps Read/Write/Edit only; `scan.js` is unchanged (specs are data, not code).
- Each round, after `validate()`: `checkWorkspaceTextures` (JS port of `checkSpec` + renderer + quality bar). HARD problems (invalid JSON/spec, file name != `name`, quality fail, more than 24) go back to the model as `repair-asset` feedback; SOFT ones (reserved namespace literal missing from the Java, a texture no string literal references, a foreign `nx_` namespace) once. Bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS` (default 2) and the overall `MB_MAX_REPAIRS`; afterwards a still-failing spec is DROPPED (file deleted, `assetDowngrades`, a warning and a "Good to know" limitation), never shipped.
- `finish()` adds `assetResult: { namespace, promptVersion, qualityVersion, kept, textures: [{ name, path, sha256 (canonical JSON), spec, quality }], downgraded, warnings }`. Specs are part of the persisted source (`files`, `source.zip`).
- Image: `textures.js` and `texture-example.json` must be in the next image, and the registry mounted at `MB_REGISTRY` or `/opt/mb/app/registry.json` (it already is for the JDK map).

### 3. Quality bar v1 (`lib/cyrus/textures/quality.ts` == `textures.js textureQuality`, version `tq-1`)
Runs on the rendered pixels of every texture (service and portal):

| Check | Pass | Warn | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| transparency | only alpha 0/255, coverage 0.10-0.85 | coverage < 0.10 or > 0.85 | any semi-transparent pixel, coverage < 0.04, or every pixel solid |
| palette_size (distinct colours) | <= 32 / 48 / 64 at 16 / 32 / 64 px | above that | > 48 / 96 / 128 |
| contrast (WCAG ratio darkest vs lightest) | >= 2.5 | 1.6-2.5 | < 1.6 |
| noise (grain: neighbour pairs differing by 1-24 RGB) | <= 0.20 | 0.20-0.35 | > 0.35 |
| outline (dark silhouette pixels) | >= 50 % | below (Style DNA hint only) | never |
| vanilla_lookalike | | | `not_run` stub: needs the vanilla texture set on the build host (GAPS 15) |

Calibrated on the existing reference specs: ruby sword and health potion pass; the Glock (49 colours at 32 px) and the frost blades (noise) warn. Golden fixtures: `test/fixtures/cyrus-textures/` (`ruby_sword` pass, `flat_square` / `tiny_dot` / `noisy_orb` fail), plus a pinned render hash. The report is stored with every asset. The vision-model judge and owner gallery are later (R1 day 8).

### 4. Portal sync (`lib/cyrus/assets/{textures,sync,sync-deps}.ts`, hook in `lib/modbuilder/store.ts`)
When the service reports `succeeded` with an `assetResult`, before the row flips to succeeded (a DB error throws, so the next sync retries): re-validate + render + quality each spec with the TypeScript code (the service is not trusted; failures are dropped), `buildPack` for the build's version (**no allowPreview**: 26.x packs are refused until the registry marks them verified), `publishPack` to `selectPackStore()` (a storage error never blocks the plugin: status `unhosted`), the Pack Loader entry with `applyPackChange` (role `main`, prompt "<plugin> uses custom item textures. Accept the pack to see them.", `required: false`), one `CyrusRevision` (kind `generated`, status `passed`, manifest `plugin/<jar>` artifact + `assets/textures/<name>.json` asset (sha256 of canonical JSON) + `resourcepack/<sha1>.zip` resourcePack, engine record with the asset prompt version and toolchain) and one `CyrusProjectAsset` per texture (mime `application/vnd.nxeon.texture-spec+json`, provenance = spec, quality report, PNG sha256, pack sha1, build id). Stored in `ModBuild.result.assets` (`MbAssets`, customer-visible): `status` ready / unhosted / none / failed, textures with their model keys, dropped, pack (sha1, sha256, bytes, format, clientVerified, url), loader entry, notices.
Idempotent: the revision is found by `modBuildId` (appends use `expectedHeadId`; a `stale_head` loser looks again), asset rows are content-addressed, the pack object is immutable. Tested with three concurrent first syncs: one revision, one asset row.

### 5. Install (`lib/cyrus/assets/{deliver,deliver-worker}.ts`, hook in `worker/game-mods.ts`)
After the Mods engine installs/updates/removes a Cyrus mod's jar, `afterCyrusModChange` (worker, same guest connection): `ensureManagedPlugin(nxeon-pack-loader, dependent project:<id>)` with the real engine installer, then upsert this mod's entry in `plugins/NxeonPackLoader/packs.json` (`writeLoaderConfig`, https only, no write when unchanged); a version without a pack drops the stale entry; removal drops the entry and releases the loader. A newly installed loader marks the job restart-required. **OFF**: unless `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` it returns before any DB read or server access, and a delivery problem is only reported, never fails the jar change. Turning that one flag on (after the owner steps below) is the only switch.

### 6. NxLabs page (`lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts assetLines`, `CyrusModView` "Custom assets")
Generated from the current version only: "Includes N custom textures; players accept a resource pack on join." (or "... delivery to servers is not switched on yet, so players don't see them yet." / "... could not be built for this version"), dropped textures, and always "Bedrock players (Geyser/Floodgate) see vanilla looks: the custom textures are a Java Edition resource pack." The studio UI is not part of this slice.

### Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-assets.test.ts` (69: the 8 plans x 6 requests gate matrix with call counting, client cannot force, 1.21.1 refusal, project reuse / failure, keep notice, detection; prompt section absent/identical vs present; JS == TS `checkSpec` on 26 inputs (18 invalid), byte-identical render and identical quality reports on 8 specs; golden quality; pack build + LocalDiskStore round trip, re-sync idempotency, unhosted / preview / dropped / namespace-mismatch; delivery switches; page lines), `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` (10, 6 new: texture build succeeds with specs + section + namespace + Read/Write/Edit only; invalid spec -> one asset repair; ugly spec -> 2 repairs then dropped with warning; not allowed -> no section, file removed, no `assets` in the record; change without rights keeps the spec sha; malformed `assets` 400). Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite: 811/811 (a first full run had one file-level failure of `cyrus-admin.test.ts` that passed alone and on the rerun: flaky under load, not touched here). `devhost tsc` clean.
- RAN on the throwaway DB (`devhost db push`, then `CYRUS_ASSETS_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-assets-db.test.ts`): 3/3 (real `tierOf` with CyrusPlan rows: free/katara/saka/lapsed refused, all + admin comp allowed with a real `nx_` project reused by the change; sync with the real store: 1 revision, head and last-passing set, quality in provenance, concurrent first syncs; delivery with the real managed service + memory installer + local fake guest: added, unchanged, removed, refCount 0).
- RAN real Test Flights on node-2, one at a time (`tsx test/cyrus-assets-real.ts all --out ...`; raw results `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/assets-r1-flights-2026-10-10.json`): Pack Loader fixture jar + `TfItemModel` fixture (does what generated mods do: `setItemModel(new NamespacedKey(ns, name))`, built with `fixtures/build.sh` against the 1.21.11 classpath, api-version 1.21.4; also compiled clean against 26.2) + the `packs.json` produced from the synced pack exactly as `deliverBuildPack` writes it.

| Flight | Pack | Result | Boot | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1.21.11 b132 / JDK 21 | production `syncBuildAssets` path, format 75, 2 textures (quality pass) | passed 6/6: `nxpacks list` 1 pack with the sha1, `config=ok`, `/tfitem` -> `itemModel=nx_r1fl1ght:ruby_sword` and `:health_potion`, both plugins green | 18.4 s | 875 MB |
| Paper 26.2 b133 / JDK 25 | `buildPack(allowPreview)` in the TEST only (format 88; production refuses preview) | passed 6/6, same checks | 10.4 s | 809 MB |

  No process with a run marker and an empty `runs/` afterwards. Fixture jar: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight/inbox/fx/TfItemModel-1.0.0.jar` (sha256 3930e6a7...85f8).
- **NOT RUN**: no real Minecraft client (server-side only): the pack download, the accept prompt and the textures actually showing are unverified (`resourcePackClientVerified` stays false). No real model build (no paid AI): Claude's real pixel quality is unmeasured (C-texture: a 30-sample eval is needed). No real bucket, domain, customer server or production DB. The real engine installer was not pointed at a server.

### Sound slice interface (where sounds plug in)
Built: see "Cyrus sound slice (R1)" below for what was implemented (one spec file per sound SET rather than per event).
1. `lib/cyrus/assets/plan.ts`: set `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY.sound = true`. The gate (Saka+), the request detection (`custom_sound` rule), the service flag (`assets.sound`, already parsed and recorded) and the notices need no change.
2. Service: a `SOUND_SECTION` in `prompts.js` appended when `rec.assets.sound`; spec files `assets/sounds/<event>.json` (a `SoundSpec`: events -> layers -> processing, library refs by id) added to the `sanitizeWorkspace` allow-list under the same keep rule; a `checkWorkspaceSounds` beside `checkWorkspaceTextures` returning `{ problems, soft, results }`, run by `assetRound` (shares `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS` and the drop-don't-ship downgrade); `assetResult.sounds: [{ key, path, sha256, spec, quality }]` next to `textures`. Plugin rule: play `Sound.sound(Key.key(ns, event))`-style namespaced keys from `sounds.json`, never override vanilla keys.
3. Portal: `SvcAssetResult.sounds`; in `syncBuildAssets` render each sound (server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis mono Ogg), quality (mono, true peak, loudness band, silence ratio), add `assets/<ns>/sounds/*.ogg` + `sounds.json` (with mandatory subtitle keys) to the SAME pack (extend `buildPack` to take `sounds`), `recordAsset(kind "sound")`, manifest role `asset`; `MbAssets.sounds`. Hosting, the Pack Loader entry, the revision, delivery and the page lines are shared (one pack per mod, role `main`).

### Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- Pack entries are `required: false`: a player who declines sees missing-model items instead of being kicked. Change to `true` per mod if the owner prefers.
- `existing` textures count as requested on a change, so a top-plan change can edit them; a lower plan gets "kept exactly as they are".
- Quality thresholds above (v1, calibrated on the 4 reference specs); the outline check only warns.
- Soft cross-checks (namespace literal / unreferenced texture) get one repair and then become warnings, because a plugin may build keys from parts; hard failures are dropped.
- A storage error leaves the plugin shipped with status `unhosted` (no automatic re-publish yet).
- Revision kind is `generated` also for kept (unchanged) textures; `message` says "(kept unchanged)".
- `PROMPT_VERSION` was left unchanged so non-asset builds keep their dedupe keys; asset builds carry `mb-assets-2026-10-10.1`.

### Owner actions (nothing needed to merge; all needed before customers see textures)
1. R0 items first: apply the engine-core and managed-plugin migrations, seed the catalog, choose pack storage + an Nxeon pack domain (`CYRUS_PACK_STORE=s3`, `CYRUS_PACK_S3_*`, `CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`), put the Pack Loader jar on the worker host.
2. Rebuild the build-service image with `textures.js` + `texture-example.json` (VM 88001 untouched by this branch).
3. A real-client test day (T) on 1.21.11 and 26.x: accept the pack, see the ruby sword; then set `resourcePackClientVerified`.
4. Approve a small paid eval (about 30 texture prompts) before promising texture quality.
5. Then `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` on the worker is the only switch for delivery.
