## Cyrus gameplay designers (R3)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r7` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 1, 2, 2b, 4.1, 4.3 and R3 "Gameplay Designers" (Custom Item Designer + typed ability/event graph + verified component library); research `A-content.md` (items/abilities/projectiles are vanilla-client possible, high AI reliability) and `F-quality-market.md` (verified recipes over free-form code). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** One flag, OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (portal: a build request may get the designer route). Off, nothing is decided or recorded and every build request is byte-identical to before. **Not plan-gated** (owner decision): no plan lookup happens for the designer; any texture / sound / model a design references still goes through the existing asset gates (the texture route needs the top plan, sounds Saka+; without the asset the item keeps its base look / the sound key plays nothing). Installing and keeping are never gated. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the designer lives in `lib/cyrus/designer` and only uses `lib/cyrus/{datapack,engine-core,versions}`); no new tables, no foreign keys; designs are stored in the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "design"`.

**The idea.** Common mechanics (a weapon that marks enemies, a staff with charges and a projectile, a tonic with a timed buff) never need free-form AI Java: the model writes a typed `ItemDesign` (data), Nxeon validates it like code and **compiles** it deterministically into a complete Paper plugin that calls a fixed, reviewed component library. Every number, text and sound key of the graph becomes a `config.yml` parameter, so a later change of cooldown / range / strength / sound changes config.yml only: no regeneration, no model call, not one Java file.

### 1. Files
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/cyrus/designer/spec.ts` | the design IR (Zod): `ItemDesignSchema`, `CAPS`, `BUDGET`, `DESIGN_LIMITS`, curated catalogs, `designFeatures(version)`, `validateDesign` / `validateDesigns` (never throw: `{ ok, design, errors, warnings, checks, budgets }`), `budgetOf`, `walkActions` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/designer.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema, carries every cap), generated |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/components/java.ts`, `components/index.ts` | the verified component library (Java sources + metadata: purpose, families, limits, tests), the per-version `Compat` adapter, `libraryHash()` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/compile.ts` | `compileDesigns(designs, ctx)` -> plugin sources + plugin.yml + config.yml + README, deterministic; parameter collection (`designParams`), `nextConfigVersion` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/params.ts` | the edit path: `describeParameters`, `applyParameterEdits`, `recompileWithEdits`, `diffCompiled`, `planDesignEdit` (deterministic change-request parser) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/simulate.ts` | the TS reference simulator of the graph semantics (`DesignSimulator`, `JavaRandom`) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/route.ts` | `decideDesignerRoute`, `matchDesignerWords`, `hasDesigns`, flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDesigns` (portal re-validation + re-compile, `serviceAgreed`) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |
| `services/modbuilder/designs.js` | service side: list/snapshot/check designs, asset keys of the workspace, `compileWorkspaceDesigns` |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-spec.js` | GENERATED bundle of the TS validator + compiler (734 KB incl. zod and the id lists) |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-example.json` | the prompt example (= the Void Reaper fixture, namespace `nx_abcd1234`) |
| `scripts/cyrus/build-designer-artifacts.ts` | writes the bundle + JSON Schema (`--check`, `--out-dir DIR`: run through devhost with an out-dir on node-2 and copy back) |
| `scripts/cyrus/designer-golden.ts` | prints the golden compile record (`test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/golden.json`) |
| `test/cyrus-designer.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-designer-real.ts`, `test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/` | pure suite, real node-2 runner, the three designs + golden hashes |

Changed: `services/modbuilder/{server.js,prompts.js,textures.js,Dockerfile}`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{request,sync}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/meta.ts`, `lib/modbuilder/{create,types,client}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/engine-core/store.ts` (asset kind `design`), `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts`.

### 2. The design IR (ItemDesign v1)
One file per item, `assets/designs/<id>.json`, at most 6 per mod. `{ schemaVersion: 1, id, base: "minecraft:<item>", name: {text, color?}, lore?, rarity?, glint?, assets?: { model?: "<ns>:<texture name>", sounds?: [keys] }, stats?: { damage + attackSpeed together, durability?, unbreakable? }, passives?: [{effect, amplifier?, slot}], marks?: [{name, durationTicks, maxPerOwner, glow?}], abilities: [0-6], permissions?: [{node, description, default}], recipe?, acquisition?: { loot?: [{table, chance}], drops?: [{entity, chance}] } }`. Unknown keys are refused. The item's identity is `<ns>:<id>` (PersistentDataContainer, never name/lore).
- **Ability** = `{ id, name, trigger, conditions?, actions, cooldownTicks?, charges?: {max, regenTicks}, manualCooldown?, manualCharges?, feedback? }`. Own cooldown and charges are checked before the conditions and spent when the ability fires (unless manual).
- **Triggers**: `right_click` / `sneak_right_click` (`targetRange?`: ray trace for a target entity + aim point), `left_click_hit_entity`, `kill_entity`, `projectile_hit` (`tag` of a `launch_projectile` of the same item), `held_interval` (`periodTicks` >= 10, main hand or inventory), `join`, `death` (fires for the dead player), `item_consume` (edible/drinkable base only), `charge_release` (hold sneak to charge, release by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; `minChargeTicks`, `maxChargeTicks`; actions may `scaleWithCharge`).
- **Conditions** (all must pass, `negate?` on each; a condition about a missing target is always false): `cooldown_ready`, `has_permission` (declared node `<ns>.<node>`), `target_is` (kinds player/hostile/animal/living and/or vanilla entity types), `world_in`, `health_below` / `health_above` (self/target, fraction), `item_identity` (main/off hand holds a design item), `sneaking`, `charges_available`, `random_chance` (java.util.Random seeded with `general.random_seed`), `time_of_day`.
- **Actions**: `damage` (player as the source: PvP and protection plugins apply), `heal`, `potion_effect` (31 curated effects), `knockback`, `pull_to` (self/point), `push_from`, `teleport_short` (self only, safe-spot search), `launch_projectile` (snowball/arrow/small_fireball/wind_charge; tagged, removed after its lifetime, arrows not pickable, fireballs non-incendiary yield 0), `spawn_particles` (28 data-free particles), `play_sound` (namespaced key only), `send_message` / `actionbar` / `title` (plain text + colour, `{player}` `{target}`), `give_item` (vanilla or own design item), `set_cooldown`, `consume_charge`, `apply_mark`, `query_marked` and `query_nearby` (bounded loops: target = each entity), `delayed` (one scheduled step), `branch` (if/then/else). **There is no run_command** and no way to express arbitrary code.
- **Recipe**: the data pack studio's shaped/shapeless shapes (`IngredientSchema` reused: vanilla item, `#tag`, list of items) plus own design items as ingredients (`ExactChoice`); registered by the plugin (a data pack cannot give the result its PDC identity); unlocked for every player on join.

**Caps** (inclusive; the schema refuses outside them, the runtime config loader clamps to the same numbers): cooldown 0-72000 ticks; charges 1-20, regen 20-72000; targetRange 1-32 blocks; held interval 10-1200; charge min 5-200, max 10-400; damage 0-40; heal 0-20; potion 1-1200 ticks, amplifier 0-4; strength 0-3 (blocks/tick), vertical 0-1.5 (velocity also capped at 4); teleport 1-16; projectile speed 0.2-3, lifetime 20-200; particles 1-64, spread 0-4, speed 0-1; volume 0-2, pitch 0.5-2; give 1-64; charge cost 1-5; mark 20-1200 ticks, 1-32 per owner; query_marked radius 1-32, query_nearby radius 1-12, max 1-16; delay 1-100; chance / health fraction / loot chance 0-1; time 0-23999; title fades 0-40, stay 10-200; passive amplifier 0-2; stats damage 1-40, attack speed 0.25-4, durability 1-10000; texts 120 / title 40 / subtitle 60 characters. Structure: 16 actions per list, 8 conditions, 6 abilities, 48 nodes per ability, depth 3, 4 marks, 4 passives, 6 lore lines, 64 KB per file.
**Budget per activation** (static worst case must fit; the `Budget` component enforces it again at runtime, so raising a query's `max` in config.yml cannot exceed it): 64 actions, 32 entity effects, 8 scheduled steps, 512 particles, 3 projectiles. No query inside a query; no delayed / projectile / teleport inside a query. Plugin-wide: 128 live one-shot tasks, 2048 marks.
**Semantic checks** (codes in the tests): banned bases (operator items, spawn eggs, ender pearl/eye, chorus fruit, milk, bundles...), block bases with click abilities, consume on a non-edible base, damage/attackSpeed pair, unresolved abilities/marks/items/projectile tags/permissions, reserved permission nodes, vanilla ids per exact version (items, entity types, loot tables, tags), foreign namespaces, missing target for the trigger, ambiguous sneak triggers, harmful/instant passives, recipe pattern/key, self-ingredient, plugin command name = a vanilla command, two ids mapping to one Java class. Warnings: item model on 1.21.1, unresolved asset keys, vanilla sound keys (not checked against the game).
**Optional-field defaults**: knockback lift 0.35, pull 0.25, push 0.35, amplifier 0, projectile lifetime 100, particle spread 0.3 / speed 0.02, volume 1, pitch 1, title 10/40/10 ticks, give count 1, charge cost 1, passive amplifier 0.

### 3. Verified component library (`lib/cyrus/designer/components`)
Fixed Java, rendered into `<pkg>.designer`: `Trigger`, `Budget`, `Activation`, `ItemIdentity` (PDC `<ns>:item`), `Cooldowns` (per player + ability, server ticks), `Charges` (lazy regeneration, no task), `Marks` (per-owner cap with oldest replaced, plugin-wide cap, cleanup on expiry / target death / owner quit or death / disable), `Tasks` (Paper main-thread scheduler only, tracked, capped, all cancelled on disable; timers restarted on reload), `DesignConfig` (jar defaults, clamping, migration hook), `Checks`, `Targets` (ray trace, nearby sphere, nearest first, never the player, no armor stands, players only on request), `Effects` (every action), `Ability` (the fixed activation protocol: re-entry guard -> own cooldown -> own charges -> conditions -> start cooldown / spend charge -> actions), `DesignItem`, `Designer` (the hub: owns all state, drops a player's state on quit and death), `DesignListener` (the safe listener base), `DesignCommand`, and the per-version `Compat`. Each component's metadata lists its purpose, families (1.21 and 26), limits and tests.
- **Listener rules**: observation handlers run at MONITOR and never change or cancel an event; they skip events another plugin cancelled (`ignoreCancelled`), except `PlayerInteractEvent`, which Bukkit delivers already "cancelled" for right-clicks in the air: there the item-use result is checked instead (DENY = another plugin blocked it). The two handlers that ADD items (loot tables via `LootGenerateEvent`, mob drops) run at NORMAL. Main hand only; one click activation per player per tick. The re-entry guard means effects of an activation (its damage, a kill it causes) never trigger abilities again.
- **Scheduling**: Paper-only (`BukkitScheduler`, main thread). No Folia region schedulers and plugin.yml does not claim `folia-supported`; `designFeatures(v).scheduling` is `"paper"` for every registry version (the registry has no Folia lane).
- **Commands** (plugin.yml, no Brigadier): `/<plugin lowercase> give <item> [player] [count]` (`<ns>.give`), `list` and `params [item]` (`<ns>.command`), `reload` (`<ns>.reload`); all operators by default; console can use all (give needs a player name there).
- **Config migration hook**: config.yml carries `config_version` and `# designer-values: <hash>`. When the jar's `config_version` is newer than the file on the server (the design's parameters were edited in Cyrus), every value under `items.` is reset to the jar's new default (Cyrus is the source of truth for designer values), the old file is kept as `config.yml.bak-v<N>`, `general.` is kept. A recompile with unchanged values keeps `config_version`.

### 4. Compiler (`compile.ts`)
`compileDesigns(designs, { version, namespace, pluginName, customHooks?, previousConfig?, configVersion?, assets? })` -> `{ files [{path, content, sha256, role}], readme, hash, params, pkg, mainClass, command, configVersion, designerValuesHash, modelsApplied, notes, javacVerified, libraryHash }`. Package `dev.nxeon.plugins.<lowercase name>`; main class; `items/<Item>Item.java` (ItemStack: `itemName`, lore, rarity, glint, item model through `Compat`, attribute modifiers keyed in the namespace, max damage + stack size 1, PDC identity; recipe; passives every 40 ticks; loot/drops); `abilities/<Item><Ability>.java` (straight-line Java: one field per parameter loaded by `load()` through `DesignConfig`, `check()` with the conditions, `run()` with the actions, budget checks before every action, `describe()` for `/params`). Items are sorted by id, so file order does not change the output. Deterministic: same designs + context = same bytes (golden hashes for all six versions in `test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/golden.json`).
**Per-version differences** (from the javap-verified API sheets + failure rules): `Attribute.GENERIC_ATTACK_DAMAGE/ATTACK_SPEED/MAX_HEALTH` on 1.21.1 (enum), unprefixed from 1.21.3 (registry interface; `designFeatures` uses 1.21.3, the registry's first plain version is 1.21.4); `ItemMeta#setItemModel` from 1.21.4 (registry capability `itemModelDefinitions`): on 1.21.1 the item keeps its base look and the README says so; `api-version` = the exact version; JDK release 21 / 25 from the registry. Everything else is the same source on all versions (each component's text is identical across versions; a test checks it). With `assets.models` given, an item model the mod does not have is left out (the item keeps its base look instead of the missing-model checkerboard).

### 5. Edit without regenerating (`params.ts`)
Every graph value is a parameter at a stable config path: `items.<item>.abilities.<ability>.cooldown_ticks`, `.charges.max|regen_ticks`, `.trigger.target_range|period_ticks|min_charge_ticks|max_charge_ticks`, `.<node>.<field>` with node paths `a<i>` (actions), `.n<j>` (inside query/delayed), `.then<j>` / `.else<j>`, `c<i>` / `.if<j>` (conditions); item level `items.<item>.marks.<name>.*`, `.passives.p<i>.amplifier`, `.loot.l<i>.chance`, `.drops.d<i>.chance`. Structure stays code: kinds, effects, particles, targets, stats, recipe, base.
- `applyParameterEdits(designs, [{path, value}])` checks each value against the parameter's caps; `recompileWithEdits(previous, edits, ctx)` recompiles against the previous config.yml and returns the diff.
- **Demonstration (test + real run)**: editing the Void Pull cooldown 160 -> 100, target range 24 -> 30, query radius 16 -> 20, pull strength 1.2 -> 2.0 and its sound -> `minecraft:entity.warden.sonic_boom` changes exactly ONE source file (`src/main/resources/config.yml`, `config_version` 1 -> 2) plus the README text; all 27 Java files are byte-identical, and in the rebuilt jar the only differing entry is `config.yml` (every .class identical, on 1.21.11 and 26.2). A structural change (a particle) changes exactly that ability's Java file and the config labels.
- `planDesignEdit(text, designs)`: a deterministic parser for change requests that only tweak parameters ("set the void pull cooldown to 5 seconds and the pull strength to 2", "change the void pull sound to nx_x:void_reaper.boom", "set the storm bolt cooldown to 40 ticks, storm bolt charges to 5"). Seconds are the default unit for ticks; `%` and hearts convert. A clause without a name inherits the previous clause's item/ability. Anything structural ("add", "instead", "make it shoot..."), unreadable or ambiguous (two items with a sound) returns `{ kind: "model" }` with the candidates. It is a pure API: the host can apply the edits with `recompileWithEdits` and skip the model; **not wired into `create.ts`** (decision below).

### 6. Reference simulator (`simulate.ts`)
A TS twin of the runtime: same activation protocol, cooldowns in ticks, lazy charges, marks (per-owner eviction order, expiry, death cleanup), the click / sneak / charge dispatch, the static + runtime budget, the re-entry guard (a kill caused by the activation logs `kill_trigger_suppressed`), delayed steps (dropped when the player left), held_interval timers, clamped config overrides (`config` option), and `JavaRandom` (a port of java.util.Random: the same seed gives the same `random_chance` sequence as the plugin; checked against real Java 21 on node-2). It logs effects (damage/heal/potions/velocity vectors/particles/sounds/texts/marks/branches); physics, real ray tracing, protection plugins and clients are NOT simulated.

### 7. Build service, router, portal
- **Router** (`route.ts`, called from `lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts` like the data pack route): with the flag on, a request with an item word (sword, staff, wand, tonic, potion, relic, bow, ...) AND an ability word (cooldown, right-click, charge, mark, pull, dash, teleport, projectile, buff, heal, on hit, on kill, passive, ...), `assets: ["design"]`, or a base build that has designs -> `service.assets.design = true` + the project namespace (a project is created if needed), `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.designer = { route, matched, limits }`. An unsupported version (26.3) gets a notice and no route.
- **Service**: `assets.design` parsed (non-boolean = 400; off with a note on unsupported versions); the `ITEM DESIGNER` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text; namespace in the user turn); allow-list `assets/designs/<id>.json`; a change build without the route keeps the base's designs byte for byte. Each round, BEFORE validate(): `designRound` validates every design with the generated bundle (+ the workspace's texture/sound keys); hard problems go back as a `design` repair (shared `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`); afterwards failing designs are dropped (customer-visible) and the rest re-checked; the valid ones are COMPILED into the workspace: generated sources replace every Java file outside `<pkg>.custom` and the plugin.yml / config.yml (free-form Java only in `custom/`, entry `CustomHooks.enable(JavaPlugin)` / `disable()`, wired into the main class when present). No valid design = the build fails clearly (never a half mod). Then the normal validate / precheck / javac / strict scan run on the generated code. `assetResult.designs` + `designCompile` (hash, config_version, settings, README, notes) + `designPromptVersion` `mb-design-2026-10-10.1`; `rec.config` lists the settings when the model's summary has none; designer builds are never deduped; `/health` lists `design`. The image needs `designer-spec.js`, `designs.js`, `designer-example.json` (Dockerfile updated).
- **Portal sync** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` + `designer/sync.ts`): every returned design is re-validated and the whole mod re-compiled with the TypeScript compiler (the service's `configVersion`, `customHooks` and applied models reproduced); `serviceAgreed` = the hashes match; one manifest row `assets/designs/<id>.json` (role `asset`) and one `CyrusProjectAsset` (`kind design`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.item-design+json`, provenance = spec, compiler, library hash, compile hash, config_version, serviceAgreed, javacVerified) per design; `MbAssets.designs`. Idempotent like the other assets.

### 8. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-designer.test.ts` 75/75 (every one of the 40 caps at min/max accepted and just outside refused; 30+ semantic error codes; static budgets; JSON Schema current; components present + documented; golden hashes on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11/26.1.2/26.2 and order independence; per-version differences; generated code free of reflection/threads/network/commands and clean under the strict source rules and the service's precheck rules for every version; config.yml/plugin.yml/README; custom hooks; unresolved models; parameter edits touch only config.yml; structural edit touches one Java file; edit refusals; the change-request parser; simulator scenarios for all three designs + permissions/negate/re-entry/runtime budget/clamping + held_interval/join/death; JavaRandom; TS == generated JS on fixtures + broken corpus for 3 versions; artifacts current; prompt section; routing; not-plan-gated request; portal sync). `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` 24/24 (4 new: designer build compiles the design into the workspace with the model's main + plugin.yml replaced and custom hooks kept, service hash == TypeScript; an out-of-cap value -> one design repair -> ships; a design that keeps failing -> dropped -> clear failure; not routed -> file removed, malformed flag 400). Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite 1249: 1246 passed, 3 failed in the first run = the image COPY test (fixed: Dockerfile) and `cyrus-admin.test.ts` (passes alone; known flaky under load). `tsc` clean.
- RAN REAL on node-2 (`devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-designer-real.ts --out ...`; raw: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/designer-r3-flights-2026-10-10.json`), one flight at a time:

| Lane | javac (27 sources, -Xlint:deprecation,removal) | Catalog (28 particles, 31 effects, 25 bases, 4 projectiles) | Jar | Strict scan | Test Flight | Edit jar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.11 / JDK 21.0.12 / Paper b132 | ok, 0 warnings, 1.4 s | compiles | 70 KB, reproducible | 0 blocks, 0 warnings (bytecode + source) | passed 6/6, boot 17.5 s, 857 MB | passed 6/6; only `config.yml` differs; migrated 1 -> 2 |
| 26.2 / JDK 25.0.4 / Paper b133 | ok, 0 warnings, 1.4 s | compiles | 70 KB, reproducible | 0 blocks, 0 warnings | passed 6/6, boot 13.8 s, 782 MB | passed 6/6; only `config.yml` differs; migrated 1 -> 2 |

  RCON evidence per flight: `plugins` lists VoidArsenal; `help voidarsenal` shows the plugin.yml command; `/voidarsenal` lists the three items; `/voidarsenal list` = `identity=ok`, the right material, ability count and `recipe=registered` for all three (so every ItemStack was built at runtime: names, lore, rarity, glint, item model, attribute modifiers, max damage, PDC); `give` from the console -> usage, to an offline player -> "not online", unknown item -> refused; `params` shows the defaults; an out-of-range config.yml (strength 99, cooldown -5, a bad sound key) + `/voidarsenal reload` -> clamped to 3.0 / 0 / the default key (logged as WARN, never an error); a config.yml with `config_version: 0` -> "migrated from version 0 to 1 ... backup config.yml.bak-v0" and the defaults back; on disk: config.yml written by the plugin and the backup present; no ERROR line from the plugin (4 sandbox no-internet lines, ignored by Test Flight). The edit flight boots the parameter-edited jar over the OLD config.yml: the plugin migrates it to `config_version 2` and `/params` shows cooldown 100, range 30, strength 2.0, the new sound. java.util.Random on JDK 21 printed the same sequences the simulator test asserts. Afterwards: empty `runs/`, no marker process.
- **NOT RUN**: no real Minecraft client and no bot: **gameplay behaviour was not verified in a game** (clicks, hits, marks, pulls, projectiles, particles, sounds, potions, teleports, recipes in a crafting grid, loot injection, passives); the simulator covers the logic, not the game. javac was not run for 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 26.1.2 (no resolved classpath on the build host): those sources follow the API sheets and the failure rules (`javacVerified: false` in every compile result); in particular the 1.21.1 `GENERIC_` Compat variant is unverified by javac. No real model build (fake CLI only, no paid AI): how well a real model writes designs is unmeasured. No customer server, no production DB, no migration, no deploy.

### 9. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- One ItemDesign per file; at most 6 items per mod; the designer owns the main class, plugin.yml and config.yml; free-form Java only in `<pkg>.custom` (CustomHooks); custom code cannot add commands (plugin.yml is generated).
- Every numeric/text/sound value is a config parameter (auto paths), instead of asking the model to name parameters; structure stays code. Parameter defaults live only in the jar's config.yml (Java has the caps, not the values), which is why edits never touch Java.
- Designer values are reset on a `config_version` bump (Cyrus is the source of truth), with a backup; hand edits of designer values survive reloads but not a Cyrus edit of the same mod.
- `charge_release` = hold sneak to charge (no client mod, no experimental data components), released by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; an item cannot have both sneak_right_click and a right-click release.
- Item-consume abilities run at MONITOR, so a cooldown does not stop the item being eaten (no refund).
- Stats (damage, attack speed, durability) and the recipe are code, baked into items when they are created (changing them later does not alter items players already hold).
- Unresolved own-namespace item models are left out of the jar; unresolved sound keys are only warnings.
- No query nesting and no delayed/projectile/teleport inside a query (bounded fan-out); damage uses the player as the source so PvP/protection plugins decide; teleport is self-only.
- `planDesignEdit` is exposed as a pure API and NOT wired into the build request: skipping the model for a change changes billing/revision semantics (a "build" without the service) and needs an owner decision and a service endpoint that rebuilds from edited designs.

- **Listener rules**: observation handlers run at MONITOR and never change or cancel an event; they skip events another plugin cancelled (`ignoreCancelled`), except `PlayerInteractEvent`, which Bukkit delivers already "cancelled" for right-clicks in the air: there the item-use result is checked instead (DENY = another plugin blocked it). The two handlers that ADD items (loot tables via `LootGenerateEvent`, mob drops) run at NORMAL. Main hand only; one click activation per player per tick. The re-entry guard means effects of an activation (its damage, a kill it causes) never trigger abilities again.

- **Config migration hook**: config.yml carries `config_version` and `# designer-values: <hash>`. When the jar's `config_version` is newer than the file on the server (the design's parameters were edited in Cyrus), every value under `items.` is reset to the jar's new default (Cyrus is the source of truth for designer values), the old file is kept as `config.yml.bak-v<N>`, `general.` is kept. ### 9. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- One ItemDesign per file; at most 6 items per mod; the designer owns the main class, plugin.yml and config.yml; free-form Java only in `<pkg>.custom` (CustomHooks); custom code cannot add commands (plugin.yml is generated).
- Every numeric/text/sound value is a config parameter (auto paths), instead of asking the model to name parameters; structure stays code. Parameter defaults live only in the jar's config.yml (Java has the caps, not the values), which is why edits never touch Java.
- Designer values are reset on a `config_version` bump (Cyrus is the source of truth), with a backup; hand edits of designer values survive reloads but not a Cyrus edit of the same mod.
- `charge_release` = hold sneak to charge (no client mod, no experimental data components), released by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; an item cannot have both sneak_right_click and a right-click release.
- Item-consume abilities run at MONITOR, so a cooldown does not stop the item being eaten (no refund).
- Stats (damage, attack speed, durability) and the recipe are code, baked into items when they are created (changing them later does not alter items players already hold).

input.message:
I built the gameplay designer engine (backend only) on `feature/cyrus-r7`. tsc is clean, all tests pass, the real node-2 runs passed, and it is committed in 9 commits. Nothing is deployed and the flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` is off; no real client and no bot were used, so gameplay itself was not tested in a game.

**What I built** (in `lib/cyrus/designer/`)
- `spec.ts` is the item design format plus the ability graph: 10 triggers, 11 conditions and 21 actions. There is no `run_command`. All 39 number types have hard limits, also written into the JSON Schema. Each activation has a budget, checked when a design is validated and again at runtime: 64 actions, 32 entity effects, 8 scheduled steps, 512 particles, 3 projectiles.
- `components/` holds the 17 fixed Java components, including item identity stored on the item, per-player cooldowns and charges, marks, a config loader that clamps values and migrates old files, a safe event listener, the scheduler helper, target selection, the effects and the `/<mod> give|list|params|reload` command. Only one small version file (`Compat`) changes per Minecraft version.
- `compile.ts` turns designs into the full plugin, the same output every time (golden hashes for 6 versions), with an 'edit without rebuilding' path in `params.ts`, a TS simulator in `simulate.ts`, routing in `route.ts` and the portal re-check in `sync.ts`.
- The build service (`designs.js`, a generated `designer-spec.js` bundle, a DESIGN prompt section) checks designs, sends errors back to the model a limited number of times, drops bad designs and compiles the rest before the normal javac and safety scan.

**What ran**
- 75 new pure tests and 4 new build-service pipeline tests; the whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite is 1279/1279.
- On node-2: javac on 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25) with 0 warnings, reproducible jars, strict scan with 0 findings, and every Test Flight passed 6/6.
- Over RCON: give, list (the items are really built on the server), params, out-of-range config values clamped, an old config_version migrated with a backup.
- Results file: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/designer-r3-flights-2026-10-10.json`.

**Edit without regenerating, shown on both versions:** changing the Void Pull's cooldown, range, pull strength and sound changes only `config.yml`; every .class file in the jar is identical. Booting that edited jar over the old config migrated it to version 2 with the new values.

**Not run**
- No in-game test of clicks, pulls, projectiles, recipes or loot.
- No javac on 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8 or 26.1.2 (no classpath on node-2), so the 1.21.1 attribute-name variant is unverified.
- No real model build.

**Decisions I made**
- The designer owns the main class, `plugin.yml` and `config.yml`. Free-form Java goes only in `custom/`, and it cannot add commands.
- Every number, text and sound becomes a config setting automatically.
- When a design changes, Cyrus overwrites the server's designer settings; the old file is kept as a backup.
- Charged abilities work by holding sneak and releasing.
- A build fails if no valid design is left (no fallback to free-form Java).
- The parser that spots "just tweak a setting" requests (`planDesignEdit`) is exposed but not wired in: skipping the model changes billing, so that is your call.

Everything is documented in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` under "Cyrus gameplay designers (R3)".
